newsitem.title: UK: Blair hails new era for Anglo-American ties.
newsitem.headline: Blair hails new era for Anglo-American ties.

text.p: Prime Minister Tony Blair and President Bill Clinton heaped praise on each other on Thursday and agreed that Britain's warming ties with Europe could only help strengthen its relations with the United States.

Minutes after welcoming Clinton and his wife Hillary in warm sunshine to his Downing Street residence, Blair invited the president to join the weekly meeting of his cabinet -- an honour previously given only to President Richard Nixon in 1969.
"I hope that this does usher in a new time of understanding and cooperation between our two countries, which have such strong bonds of history and heritage together," Blair said.

"I want to say how absolutely delighted I am on a personal level to welcome you here because we believe that the courage and strength of leadership you have shown in the United States have brought enormous benefits not just to your own country but to the world," he added.

Since he was elected by a landslide on May 1, Blair has started to repair relations with Europe that frayed badly as the former Conservative government became increasingly hostile to European Union (EU) plans for closer integration.
But Blair, in opening remarks that were carried on television, told Clinton Britain did not have to choose between a strong relationship with Europe and one with Washington.
"I think the one strength deepens the other. A Britain that is leading in Europe is a Britain capable of ever closer relations also with the United States of America," he said.

Clinton, whose relations with former prime minister John Major were no better than cordial, replied: "I agree that it is good for the United States to have a Britain that is strong in Europe and strong in its relations with the United States."

The president, the first foreign leader to phone Blair after his landslide election victory on May 1, thanked him for being invited to address the cabinet and said he admired the brisk start his government had made.

"I have watched with enormous interest the energy and vigour with which you have all taken office and the optimism with which you pursue it," Clinton, seated between Blair and Cabinet Secretary Sir Robin Butler, said.
"This is a very exciting time and I am glad to be here."

Clinton, who flew to London after a NATO-Russia summit in Paris and a U.S.-EU summit in The Hague, spoke of the need to "create within Europe a continent that is democratic, undivided and at peace for the first time ever".
He said: "Europe has been periodically at peace but never all democratic and certainly never undivided".

The mutual compliments underscored the warm personal relationship that British officials say "Bill and Tony" had already struck up before the visit, which Clinton has extended to a full day to give him more time to chat and socialise.

Asked by a reporter whether he had any advice for Blair, Clinton joked: "He is doing very well. I would like to have a 179-seat majority. I am not going to give any advice. I am going to sit here and take it."
As his cabinet ministers laughed, Blair said he would like to emulate Clinton, who easily won re-election last November.
"I would like to make sure we have a second term of office," Blair said with a broad smile.
Clinton had a special word for Northern Ireland Secretary Mo Mowlam, who is leading efforts to revive stalled talks over the future of the troubled British province.
"I saw you on televison last night being optimistic about peace in Ireland, which is an article of faith in my life and household -- so I like that," Clinton said.
Clinton was applauded by staff and the cabinet when he arrived and after his brief remarks ministers banged the cabinet table with their hands to show their approval.
Officials said Northern Ireland, Bosnia, NATO and Europe were among the topics Blair and Clinton were due to discuss in private talks and over lunch.
After a news conference in the Downing Street rose garden, Clinton has set aside several hours of private time to go sightseeing and have dinner with the Blairs.
